question: {If } (1)/(1 - tan theta) + (1)/(1 + tan theta) = 3, { and } theta { is an acute angle, find the value of } csc theta.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

1/(1 − tanθ) + 1/(1 + tanθ) = 3

⇒ ( (1 + tanθ) + (1 − tanθ) ) / (1 − tan²θ ) = 3

⇒ 2 / (1 − tan²θ) = 3

⇒ 1 − tan²θ = 2/3 ⇒ tan²θ = 1/3

⇒ tanθ = 1/√3 (acute angle)

⇒ sinθ = 1/2 ⇒ cscθ = 2

**∴ Answer = 2**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

1/(1 − tanθ) + 1/(1 + tanθ) = 3

**Formula used:**

(a/b + c/d) = (ad + bc)/bd

**Calculation:**

⇒ Combine fractions:

⇒ ( (1 + tanθ) + (1 − tanθ) ) / (1 − tan²θ ) = 3

⇒ 2 / (1 − tan²θ) = 3

⇒ 1 − tan²θ = 2/3

⇒ tan²θ = 1/3

⇒ Since θ is acute:

⇒ tanθ = 1/√3

⇒ Using standard triangle:

Opp = 1, Adj = √3 ⇒ Hyp = 2

⇒ sinθ = 1/2

⇒ cscθ = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Identity Used

1 − tan²θ = cos²θ − sin²θ relation

Triangle Method

Use right triangle for trig ratios

Acute Angle Condition

Take positive root

Key Insight

Reduce expression to single trig ratio
